Алгоритм выполнения задания 11: 4 главных шага

Прочитайте перед чтением текста и держите в голове на каждом варианте.

1

Сначала прочитайте весь текст, чтобы понять общий смысл.

2

Разберите предложение с пропуском: время, какой член предложения пропущен, союзы, местоимения, запятые.

3

Разберите фрагменты: с какого слова начинается, какое время, какое число у существительного, какие местоимения.

4

Фрагмент должен подойти и по смыслу, и по структуре. Перечитайте текст с фрагментами и объясните, почему лишний фрагмент не подошёл.

Полный алгоритм (18 шагов)
  1. Перед тем как приступить к заполнению пропусков, следует прочитать текст полностью (просмотровое чтение), чтобы понять его общий смысл.
  2. Далее, после первичного прочтения текста, возможны два пути (и оба по-своему продуктивны, стоит определиться, какой вам больше всего подходит, помогает выполнить задание правильно): ПУТЬ первый
  3. Путь 1. Начните анализировать текст по абзацам, обращая особое внимание на грамматическую структуру предложений, где есть пропуски (gaps): - обязательно читайте и пытайтесь понять смысл и тех частей текста, которые не содержат gaps, потому что в них может содержаться важный смысл/детали, которые помогут вам вставить пропущенные фрагменты. Помните, нам важен контекст, а контекст – это не только слова вокруг этого gap, это и предложения, которые идут до него, и после; - читая предложения до и после пропущенного фрагмента, ищите/отмечайте слова, которые могут быть полезны, например, упоминания о времени (then, after, before, before that, earlier etc.), местоимения (it, that, she/her etc.), союзы и союзные слова (which, who, where, unless etc.); - обратите внимание, в каком времени идёт повествование в данном отрезке текста; - постарайтесь предугадать содержание предложения с выпущенным фрагментом, какой там может быть смысл/содержание, про что там должно говориться?
  4. Тщательно проанализируйте лексико-грамматическую структуру этого предложения и предположите, какой член предложения или какое придаточное предложение ПО СТРУКТУРЕ подойдёт к данному пропуску: - пропущенный фрагмент часто является частью придаточного предложения; подумайте, с какого союза или с какого слова может начинаться нужный фрагмент согласно структуре предложения с пропуском в тексте; - бывают случаи, когда до пропущенного фрагмента начинается перечисление однородных членов, тогда стоит искать фрагмент с продолжением такого перечисления (обратим внимание, какие члены предложения/части речи перечисляются или могут перечисляться по смыслу текста); - обратите внимание на пунктуацию в тексте: после некоторых слов ставится запятая (например, however, между компонентами перечисления), в то время как другие слова никогда на встречаются после запятой (that).
  5. Прочитайте фрагменты 1-7. Проанализируйте, какой частью или каким членом предложения является каждый фрагмент (придаточное определительное, группа сказуемого и т.д.). Подумайте, что может ему предшествовать или может идти после него в тексте – по смыслу.
  6. Проанализируйте грамматическую СТРУКТУРУ фрагментов: - обратите внимание на союз или союзное слово, с которого начинается фрагмент; - если возможно, отметьте для себя, из какого временного контекста мог быть «вырезан» данный фрагмент; - в придаточных определительных отметьте, если это возможно по форме сказуемого, существительное в каком числе оно описывает (ед.ч/мн.ч); - если в фрагменте встречаются местоимения, обратите на них особое внимание.
  7. Вернитесь к началу текста, последовательно продвигайтесь от первого предложения, подбирая подходящие по смыслу фрагменты 1-7 с учётом проведённого анализа.
  8. Убедитесь, что фрагменты соответствуют пропускам и грамматически (СТРУКТУРА), и по СМЫСЛУ.

Text 1 · Aurora

Step 1. Before you fill in the gaps

Read the whole text first. Then look at how each part 1–7 begins (who / which / that / when / where / -ing / and…) and what kind of words it needs before it. Write two or three observations.

Step 2. Fill in the gaps

1. though a visit to the engine room carries

7. protecting the territory of the harbour

The cruiser Aurora is a museum in St. Petersburg. It is a former Russian naval ship that has played an important part in the country’s history.

The Aurora was built between 1897 and 1900 at the Admiralty shipyard in St. Petersburg. The cruiser was one of the largest ships of its time. After its construction was complete, the Aurora took its place as part of the Russian 2nd Squadron in the Pacific Ocean. In May 1905, it took part in the Battle of Tsushima and was one of just a few Russian ships . After the battle in the Baltic, it returned to St. Petersburg .

The ship served during World War I. When it returned to St. Petersburg in 1916 for major repairs, the city was on the edge of revolution the 1917 February Revolution. Soon the Aurora was to play a huge part in the October revolution. The ship is famous for firing the shot the Winter Palace.

Once again in 1922, the Aurora served as a training ship. During World War II, the ship’s guns were removed to use for land defense. Unfortunately, being left defenseless it was sunk in Leningrad harbour to keep it from . The ship was brought back to the surface in 1944 and later, after extensive repairs, it was permanently anchored at the harbour and became a museum in 1957.

The Aurora is now maintained by cadets from the nearby Nakhimov Navy School. Admission is free to the public, a small fee.

The most famous are in the Algarve. With three thousand hours of sun per year and warm waters, there are beaches to suit every taste and many dreamlike resorts. Peterhof is a monument of world architecture and palace and park art. Peterhof includes a palace and park ensemble of the 18-19th centuries, . Peterhof is a city of fountains as it contains 173 fountains and 4 cascades . Each year up to 3 million people come here to enjoy the splendour of numerous fountains and the unique parks of Peterhof.

The name Peterhof was first mentioned in 1705. It was a coastal manor, close to which the construction of a grand country residence began. The original plan belonged to Peter the Great. After the brilliant victory of Russian troops over the Swedes, security of St. Petersburg both from the land . Since that time, the construction of the Peterhof residence grew immensely in scope.

According to the plan of Peter the Great, on the one hand, Peterhof was meant to be equal in splendour with the most famous royal residences in Europe, to access the Baltic Sea. Both were successfully done. The Great Palace was built on a natural hill here, . Following the plan of Peter the Great, , the Grand Cascade with the famous Samson fountain was constructed. This is still one of the most spectacular fountains in the world. In 1990 the palaces and parks of Peterhof were included in the list of the world heritage of UNESCO.

A double-decker bus is a bus that has two levels. While double-decker long-distance buses are in widespread use around the world, . Double-decker buses are popular in some European cities and in some parts of Asia, usually in former British colonies. Many towns around the world have a few that specialize in short sight-seeing tours for tourists because, as William Gladstone observed, "the way to see London is from the top of a 'bus'".

Double-decker buses are taller than other buses. They are extensively used in the United Kingdom, , removed from normal service in December 2005 - they still operate on heritage routes. Elsewhere in Europe, double-deckers are used throughout the Dublin Bus network in Ireland, where they are making a comeback on Dublin's outer suburban routes and also the streets of Cork, Limerick, Galway and Waterford. They are a common sight in Berlin, where the BVG makes extensive use of them. Double-decker long-distance coaches are also in widespread use throughout Europe.

Most buses in Hong Kong and about half in Singapore are double-deckers as well. The only areas in North America that are the western Canadian province of British Columbia and the United States city of Las Vegas. They are currently being tested in Ottawa on the express routes. The city of Davis, California, in the United States uses vintage double-decker buses for public transport. Davis, California is also home to the first vintage double-decker bus converted from diesel gasoline to run on CNG. The city of Victoria, BC, the city of Vancouver, British Columbia, and a couple of others use Dennis Tridents. A few are also used as tour buses, especially in New York. Double-deckers have also been used in Mumbai since 1937.

In Brazil, , some companies use double-decker buses. Double-deckers are not a good option for use outside the towns (most roads in Brazil are in very poor condition), and .

Double-decker buses are in widespread use in India in many of the major cities. Some double-decker buses , with no roof and shallow sides. These are popular for sightseeing tours.

The Shard is a modern glass skyscraper in London. The skyscraper is situated in the London Bridge Quarter in Southwark. It is right near the heart of London and only the river separates it from the City of London. The area is full of history: a bridge was built there by the Romans around 50 AD .

The plans for the London Bridge Tower, as the building was initially called, caused a strong protest from people for a historic neighbourhood with mostly low-rise brick buildings. They claimed the tower would cut through the neighbourhood like a shard of glass. The name “shard” stuck – “The Shard”.

When it was completed the Shard held the record as Europe’s tallest skyscraper with a height of almost 310 metres. Only a couple of months later, it was surpassed in height by Moscow’s Mercury City Tower. The Shard towers over the neighbourhood and is visible from afar. The iconic skyscraper looks particularly spectacular at night .

The building is multifunctional, with offices and a hotel on the lower floors . The top floors of the Shard are home to the “View from the Shard”, an observation deck of the city. On a clear day one can see as far as sixty kilometres. At a height of 245 metres, this is the highest public viewing gallery in London, almost twice as high as the London Eye.

The Peter and Paul Fortress in St. Petersburg, located on small Hare Island, is the historic core of the city. The history of St. Petersburg begins with the history of the fortress.

Since 1700 Russia had been fighting the Northern War against Sweden. By 1703 the lands by the Neva River were conquered. To protect them from the attacks of the Swedes it was necessary to build a strong outpost here. The fortress was founded on Hare Island 16 (27) May, 1703 by joint plan of Peter I and French engineer Joseph-Gaspard Lambert de Guerin. This day is well known .

The fortress stretches from west to east with six bastions . The Peter’s Gate on the east side, , has remained since the time of Peter I. The Peter and Paul Cathedral, emperors and the monument of Russian baroque, was completed after the death of the emperor, in 1733. The weathervane as a golden angel with a cross, , is one of the main symbols of the city. On the opposite side of the cathedral, there is the Mint building, constructed in the time of Paul I by architect A. Porto. Coinage was moved to the fortress in the time of Peter I. The Peter and Paul Fortress has never directly participated in any fighting. From the very beginning of its existence it was used as a political prison. Since 1924 the Peter and Paul Fortress has been a part of the Museum of the History of St. Petersburg.
